description: Chaos out of order - a caster who rots a target over a dozen turns and lets the decay do the killing.
_source_note: Rebuilt 6 Nov 2026 from the 38 real CoA Infinite talents (role DPS). The spec's defining hook - 'periodic damage dealt has a chance to...' - has no engine equivalent: the DoT tick path (status_effects.py:914) runs on the target with no caster handle, so there is nothing to fire a proc on. All seven such talents are re-pointed to on_damage_cast and each says so. Long dots are the spec's point and the engine pays for extending them properly: talent extensions add TICKS at full per-turn value (abilities.py:2777), unlike raising an ability's base duration. arcane_spell_damage is LIVE - corrected 6 Nov 2026 after I wrongly grepped it as dead; <school>_spell_damage is built with an f-string at abilities.py:1371, so a literal grep cannot see it.

nodes.name: Gift of the Infinite Dragonflight
nodes.description: Increases your spell damage by 39% of your Spirit.
nodes._source: CoA level 20 passive: 'Increases your spell damage by 40% of your Spirit and your spell hit rating by 3% of your Spirit.' The first half PORTS EXACTLY - spell_damage is in STAT_CONVERSION_TARGETS and spirit in STAT_CONVERSION_SOURCES. The second half is DROPPED, both ways: hit_rating is not a valid conversion target, and hit_chance_spell is set once in Character.__init__ (line 147) and never fed from bonuses, so a talent writing it is silent. Was a pure scalar on our side. A FRACTION.

nodes.name: Temporal Decay
nodes.description: Increases the damage of your periodic effects by 12%.
nodes._source: Not a single CoA talent - the tree needs an entry point for the dot identity Kyle asked for, and dot_damage is the only global periodic key the engine reads (abilities.py:1601). Stands in for CoA's Infinite Horizon clause 'your Unmake and Timerend gain an additional 20% bonus spell scaling', which cannot be built as written (there is no per-ability spell-scaling key, only flat damage). A FRACTION.

nodes.name: Warpstriker
nodes.description: Reduces the mana cost of your spells by 6%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Reduces the cost of your spells by -5% and the chance for your spells to be dispelled by 10%.' The cost half ports; all_ability_cost_pct is a FRACTION and POSITIVE MEANS A REDUCTION. The dispel-resistance half has no key and is dropped. Was a pure scalar on our side too, but of the wrong kind - this is at least the scalar CoA wrote.

nodes.name: Deconstruction
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of Unmake by 3%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases the critical strike chance of Unmake by 5%.' Ports exactly. Per-ability crit keys are in PERCENTAGE POINTS. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Time Means Nothing
nodes.description: Increases your Arcane damage by 6%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases your magic damage dealt by 3% and damage dealt by Chromatic Shard now increases the target's spell damage taken by 10% for 30 seconds.' THE MAGIC SCOPING NOW PORTS, corrected 6 Nov 2026: arcane_spell_damage is live, read via an f-string at abilities.py:1371 inside _school_damage_bonus and resolved against the school the ability actually deals. I had written this node as all_damage after grepping for the literal key and concluding it was dead - a grep cannot see a dynamically built key, and measuring it live gave a ratio of exactly 1.500. Chronomancer's whole kit is Arcane/Chromatic, so the scoped key reaches essentially everything this class casts while still being the honest translation of 'magic damage dealt'; doubled to 6% since it is now narrower than all_damage. The Chromatic Shard debuff half moves to its own node (Chromatic Shard Mastery) where it can carry a real proc. A FRACTION.

nodes.name: Anomaly Spikes
nodes.description: Your damaging spells have a 25% chance to launch an Anomaly Spike at your target.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Periodic damage dealt now has a 8% chance to launch an Anomaly Spike at your target.' LOAD-BEARING UNLOCK - chronomancer_anomaly_spike carries requires_talent and this is its only unlock node in the game; dropping it makes the ability unobtainable forever. CoA hangs this off PERIODIC DAMAGE, which does not exist as a trigger. status_effects.py:914 applies a dot with a bare self.take_damage() on the TARGET and holds no caster reference - its own THREAT GAP note says status effects store 'potency/duration/school, not a caster or engine handle' - so there is nobody to fire a proc on. Re-pointed to on_damage_cast: it fires on the Chronomancer's damaging casts instead of on their ticks, so a player who dots and waits gets nothing. This is the class's single biggest translation loss and it affects seven talents across all three trees. The chance is raised from 8% to 25% to compensate: CoA's 8% fires off every tick of every dot on every target, which in a long fight is dozens of rolls, where on_damage_cast rolls once per cast. cast_ability takes a bare ability id and the ability must be in the caster's book, which the unlock guarantees.

nodes.name: Chromatic Shard
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Chromatic Shard by 12%, and your critical strikes increase the target's spell damage taken by 10% for 4 turns.
nodes._source: CoA, Time Means Nothing's second clause: 'damage dealt by Chromatic Shard now increases the target's spell damage taken by 10% for 30 seconds.' Split onto its own node so it can carry a real proc. The trigger is on_crit rather than 'Chromatic Shard specifically' because there is no per-ability proc trigger; a crit is the closest thing to a meaningful cast and keeps the debuff from being permanent. spell_damage_taken_pct FLIPS: it is a FRACTION read raw as a talent effect (character.py:2753) but PERCENTAGE POINTS inside a status effect (monster.py:740 divides by 100), so 10 here is 10%. 30 sec -> 4 turns at ~3 sec per turn. CoA's Chromatic Shard also pierces immunities and resistances, which has no key.

nodes.name: Erosion
nodes.description: Increases the damage of your Anomaly Spikes by 12% and your periodic damage by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA's Erasion: 'Increases the chance to trigger Anomaly Spikes by 5% and their damage by 20%.' The damage half ports exactly. The trigger-chance half cannot: the chance lives on Anomaly Spikes' own proc dict and no effect key edits another node's proc chance. Replaced with dot_damage, which keeps the node about the same loop. Renamed from CoA's 'Erasion' only in that our data already had no such node - the name is CoA's. Both FRACTIONS.

nodes.name: Mind Melt
nodes.description: Your damaging spells have a 30% chance to sap the target's strength, reducing the damage they deal for 5 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Damage dealt by Melt Reality now also reduces the target's primary attributes by -3% for 15 sec, stacking 5 times.' MAX_STACKS IS REAL AND IS KEPT (status effects stack natively), but nothing can READ the stack count, so the tier-6 End of Time clause that scales off it is built differently - see that node. '-3% primary attributes' has no home: a monster reads exactly eight status stat_mods (armor, attack_power, damage_taken_pct, healing_taken_pct, magic/physical/spell_damage_taken_pct, magic_resistance) and attack_power is FLAT (Monster.ability_power_bonus: 'Flat damage/healing swing from active buffs and debuffs'). -25 per stack, -125 at five. Flat AP reduction is CoA's own house style on this class - Artificer's Erode Armaments reduces enemy attack power by a flat 208. 15 sec -> 5 turns. The trigger is not Melt Reality specifically: no per-ability proc trigger.

nodes.name: Hourglass of Eternity
nodes.description: Your damaging spells have a 20% chance to grant 25% haste for 2 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Periodic damage dealt now has a 5% chance to grant you 25% increased haste for 5 sec.' CoA hangs this off PERIODIC DAMAGE, which does not exist as a trigger. status_effects.py:914 applies a dot with a bare self.take_damage() on the TARGET and holds no caster reference - its own THREAT GAP note says status effects store 'potency/duration/school, not a caster or engine handle' - so there is nobody to fire a proc on. Re-pointed to on_damage_cast: it fires on the Chronomancer's damaging casts instead of on their ticks, so a player who dots and waits gets nothing. This is the class's single biggest translation loss and it affects seven talents across all three trees. 5% -> 20% for the same reason as Anomaly Spikes (per-cast rolls are far rarer than per-tick ones), with a 2-turn internal cooldown so it cannot chain. 5 sec -> 2 turns. haste is in PERCENTAGE POINTS, so 25.0 is 25%.

nodes.name: Distorted Time
nodes.description: Increases the duration of your periodic effects by 21%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Reduces the cooldown of Timerend by -2 sec and increases the duration of Decomposition by 3 sec.' Generalised to every dot because dot_duration_pct is live (abilities.py:2766, a FRACTION) and is the one key that makes the spec's whole point pay off: abilities.py:2777 derives per-turn damage from the ability's OWN base duration, not the talented one, so an extension adds TICKS at full value rather than thinning the same total. This is a straight damage increase, and it is the mechanism Kyle's 'Chronomancer is a lot of DoTs' instruction actually wants - unlike editing a base duration, where per_turn = total/base_duration and the total has to move too. The Timerend cooldown half is dropped: our Timerend has no cooldown to reduce. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Destabilize Time
nodes.description: Teaches Destabilize Time, shaking a target loose from the present.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Reduces enemy casting speed by -10% for 20 seconds, increasing by -10% every time they cast. Gaining stacks does not extend the duration.' LOAD-BEARING UNLOCK - chronomancer_destabilize_time carries requires_talent and this is its only unlock node. The talent itself is the unlock and nothing more: there is no caster-side speed debuff key (that gap has now cost nodes on four classes), and nothing escalates a debuff when the TARGET acts. The ability already exists in our data as a debuff and is left as authored.

nodes.name: Magic Erosion
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Decomposition by 9%, and your critical strikes leave the target 4% easier to hit with spells for 6 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Decomposition now deals 10% more damage and applies Magic Erosion to the target, increasing attackers chance to hit the target with spells by 3% for 30 seconds.' The damage half ports (raised to 15% to carry the node alone). The hit-chance half cannot: there is no recipient-side 'chance to be hit' key anywhere, so it is repriced as magic_damage_taken_pct, which is the same direction - more of the Chronomancer's damage lands on this target. That key is PERCENTAGE POINTS inside a status effect, so 4 is 4%. 30 sec -> 6 turns. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Infinity Crash
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike damage of your spells by 20% per rank.
nodes._source: Standardised 6 Nov: every caster tree carries one 5-point spell-crit-damage talent worth +100% at full rank, matching priest_shadow's Shadow Power and shaman_elemental's Elemental Fury (both WoW-accurate). Kyle: 'all caster classes should have a 5 point talent that increases their spell crit damage by 100%.'

nodes.name: Crown of Power
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Melt Reality by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the tick rate of Melt Reality by 25%.' Tick rate has no meaning in a turn-based engine - a dot ticks once per turn, full stop - and raising its duration instead would stretch a 10-turn dot past most fights. Repriced as damage, which is what a faster tick rate amounts to in CoA. Melt Reality is the spec's long dot: 'every 3 sec for 30 sec' is exactly 10 turns here. Was a pure scalar on our side. A FRACTION.

nodes.name: Black Hole
nodes.description: Increases the damage of your periodic effects by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the damage of Chromatic Shard, Melt Reality and Unmake by 15% against slowed enemies.' The conditional is dropped: nothing reads whether a target is slowed (no payload or effect key inspects a target's debuffs), and a condition that silently never fires is worse than no condition. Kept at 15% against the spec's dots instead, which covers Melt Reality and Decomposition. Was a pure scalar on our side. A FRACTION.

nodes.name: Null Orbs
nodes.description: Your critical strikes have a 35% chance to grant Null Orbs, increasing your spell critical strike chance by 15% for 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Periodic critical damage dealt now has a 20% chance to grant Null Orbs for 8 seconds. Null Orbs increases the critical damage of Chromatic Shard and Anomaly Spikes based on your spell critical strike rating.' CoA hangs this off PERIODIC DAMAGE, which does not exist as a trigger. status_effects.py:914 applies a dot with a bare self.take_damage() on the TARGET and holds no caster reference - its own THREAT GAP note says status effects store 'potency/duration/school, not a caster or engine handle' - so there is nobody to fire a proc on. Re-pointed to on_damage_cast: it fires on the Chronomancer's damaging casts instead of on their ticks, so a player who dots and waits gets nothing. This is the class's single biggest translation loss and it affects seven talents across all three trees. on_crit is the closest live trigger and keeps CoA's 'critical' half intact. The 'based on your crit rating' scaling is dropped - no stat feeds a status effect's own magnitude. 8 sec -> 3 turns. CAREFUL: crit_damage_spell is a FRACTION as a talent effect but this is a STATUS EFFECT stat_mod, where the same key is read in PERCENTAGE POINTS - hence 40, not 0.40. Authoring 0.40 here would have delivered 0.4%. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Incarnation of Chaos
nodes.description: Teaches Incarnation of Chaos, becoming chaos itself for a short time.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Transform into an Incarnate of Chaos, instantly resetting the cooldown of Chromatic Shard and causing your next cast to not incur a cooldown. In addition, your damage dealt is increased by 15% for 15 seconds.' LOAD-BEARING UNLOCK - chronomancer_incarnation_of_chaos carries requires_talent and this is its only unlock node. The ability itself already carries the damage buff; the cooldown-reset clauses live on the ability, not here. CoA's Chaos Fusion and Pure Chaos both key off this being active - Chaos Fusion is a movement mechanic (inert: no positioning) and Pure Chaos locks the player out of all spells but one on a 1-second repeat (no mechanic locks an ability set, and no proc repeats on a timer), so neither is built.

nodes.name: Chaotic Time
nodes.description: Your damaging spells have a 25% chance to reduce the cooldown of Incarnation of Chaos by 2 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'While Incarnation of Chaos is active, your Melt Reality deals 30% increased damage and replicates an additional 20%. In addition, periodic damage dealt now reduces the cooldown of Incarnation of Chaos by -1 sec.' The cooldown clause is the buildable half and it is built: reset_cooldown with an {abilities, turns} dict shaves turns rather than fully resetting (a bare list would reset outright). CoA hangs this off PERIODIC DAMAGE, which does not exist as a trigger. status_effects.py:914 applies a dot with a bare self.take_damage() on the TARGET and holds no caster reference - its own THREAT GAP note says status effects store 'potency/duration/school, not a caster or engine handle' - so there is nobody to fire a proc on. Re-pointed to on_damage_cast: it fires on the Chronomancer's damaging casts instead of on their ticks, so a player who dots and waits gets nothing. This is the class's single biggest translation loss and it affects seven talents across all three trees. The 'while Incarnation is active' conditional on the damage half is dropped - no effect key reads whether another effect is live - and the replication clause has no mechanism (no payload copies damage to other targets as a percentage). Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Timelost Power
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Discordance by 15% and your spell damage by 3%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Discordance now strikes 3 additional enemies.' Nothing adds targets to an ability - no effect key and no proc payload touches an ability's target count - so the node is repriced as damage on the same ability plus a small global, which is what three extra targets amounts to on a spec that casts Discordance as filler. Was a pure scalar on our side. Both FRACTIONS.

nodes.name: Eternity
nodes.description: While a target is rooted by your Clasp of Infinity, your damage against them is increased. Increases all damage you deal by 3%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Clasp of Infinity now increases your damage dealt to the target by 15%.' The conditional cannot be built - nothing reads a target's debuffs, so 'to the target' and 'while rooted' are both unreachable - so it lands as a flat 5% all_damage, priced down from 15% because it is now unconditional. The description keeps the flavour sentence but states the real mechanic second, so the tooltip does not promise a condition the engine will not honour. A FRACTION.

nodes.name: End of Time
nodes.description: Increases the damage of your periodic effects by 18% and your spell critical strike chance by 3%.
nodes._source: CoA has TWO talents called End of Time in this tree. The tier-5 one: 'Mind Melt now also increases the target's periodic damage taken from you by 6% per stack.' Per-stack scaling is unbuildable - nothing reads a stack count anywhere in the engine - and there is no periodic-specific damage-taken key either, so both halves fail. Repriced to the caster side as dot_damage plus crit, which keeps the node a dot payoff. (The other End of Time, 'at the end of Clasp of Infinity you launch an Anomaly Spike at affected enemies', needs an on-expiry trigger, which does not exist.) dot_damage is a FRACTION; crit_chance_spell is PERCENTAGE POINTS. The two sit in the same dict and read opposite ways.

nodes.name: Infinite Horizon
nodes.description: Increases your spell damage by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the all damage dealt by party and raid members by 3%. Does not stack with similar effects. In addition, your Unmake and Timerend gain an additional 20% bonus spell scaling.' THE PARTY HALF CANNOT BE BUILT FROM A TALENT - a talent effect never reaches an ally; only a party-targeted ABILITY does (abilities.py:2064 resolves target_type 'party' to all living allies). Guardian's auras were converted to party abilities for exactly this reason, but Chronomancer has no aura ability to hang this on, so it stays selfish and the description does not claim otherwise. The spell-scaling half has no key (only flat damage keys exist). A FRACTION.

nodes.name: Infinite Keeper
nodes.description: Increases the damage of your periodic effects by 45%. Your critical strikes have a 40% chance to launch an Anomaly Spike.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Using Unmake on an enemy affected by your Timerend now causes the enemy to erupt in a vortex of sand, dealing Chromatic Damage every 1 sec to up to 8 enemies for 6 sec in an 8 yd radius.' The combo condition is unbuildable twice over - nothing reads a target's debuffs, and there is no per-ability proc trigger - and the 8-yard radius has no positioning to stand on. Rebuilt as the capstone the spec's own tree has been building toward. ORIGINALLY THIS CARRIED +30% DOT DURATION TOO, and it was removed on 6 Nov 2026 after fight length was measured: stacked with Distorted Time's 20% it took Melt Reality to 9 turns, and a 9-turn dot delivers about a third of its damage on trash (2-3 turns) and two thirds on a boss (5-6). ONE duration node per tree is the rule now - Distorted Time keeps it, this trades its share for damage, so a fully talented Melt Reality lands at 7 turns rather than 9. dot_damage reaches the same place without pushing the dot past the window it is played in. A FRACTION.
